title: Hanuman's heart
hook: Hanuman opens his chest to show who lives there, and Patanjali sends you to the heart to know your own mind
tomorrow: Fourteen years to walk on water

segments.voice: Yesterday: Dhruva, devotion that doesn't move, set in the sky as the pole star.

The war is over. Rama is crowned in Ayodhya, and Sita gives Hanuman a gift, a necklace of pearls. Hanuman takes it, and in front of the whole court, starts biting the pearls open, one by one, peering inside each. People laugh. Someone asks what on earth he's doing. Looking for Rama, he says. Anything without Rama in it is worth nothing to me. So, they ask, is Rama in you? Hanuman tears open his chest. And there, in his heart, sit Rama and Sita.
screen: `A NECKLACE OF PEARLS.` → `BITTEN OPEN, ONE BY ONE.` → `RAMA AND SITA, IN HIS HEART.`

segments.voice: That scene isn't in Valmiki's Ramayana. It comes from later, much-loved tellings, and it's painted on calendars and temple walls wherever Hanuman is loved. It pictures one of Hinduism's deepest teachings: God lives in the heart. In the Gita, Krishna says the Lord dwells in the heart of every being. On day three fifty-six you met the Upanishad's picture: the body as the city of Brahman, and in it a small lotus-house, the heart, with a space inside as wide as the sky. Now Patanjali. After the sky and the navel, samyama climbs: 3.30, on the hollow of the throat, hunger and thirst cease; 3.32, on the light in the crown, the vision of the perfected ones. Then 3.34: hridaye chitta-samvit. In the heart, knowledge of the mind. Chitta is the whole field of thinking and feeling. Rest attention in the heart, and you come to know it. The classical commentary reads the sutra through that same lotus-house in the city of Brahman. So to know your own mind, the tradition doesn't send you to think harder. It sends you to the heart, where, many Hindus say, God is already sitting. Hanuman didn't have to argue for his love. He only had to show what lived there. And today, when you're trying to work out what you really want, ask what lives in your heart. That's what's running the mind.
screen: `NOT IN VALMIKI; LOVED EVERYWHERE.` · `THE GITA: THE LORD IN EVERY HEART.` · `THE LOTUS-HOUSE IN THE CITY.` · `3.34: IN THE HEART, KNOWLEDGE OF THE MIND.` · then, large: `GOD LIVES IN THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Put a hand on the center of your chest and feel it rise and fall. Let your attention settle there, not in the head. If you pray, picture the form of God you love seated there, the way Hanuman held Rama and Sita. If you don't, picture a small lotus with a quiet space inside. When thoughts come, watch them from the chest.
The heart. Hridaya: where samyama gives knowledge of the mind, and where Hanuman kept Rama and Sita.
Your line: God lives in the heart. Hanuman only had to open his. Day four seventy-two, done.

screen: `DAY 472 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: FOURTEEN YEARS TO WALK ON WATER.`

howItsDone: Many Hindus meditate on their chosen form of God seated in the heart, and pictures of Hanuman opening his chest to show Rama and Sita hang in homes and temples; teachers of the Yoga Sutras read 3.34 alongside the Upanishads' lotus of the heart.
